steps.title: Find the Clio developer portal and OAuth documentation
steps.detail: Locate Clio's developer portal and its OAuth documentation, then record the app-registration URL, authorization and token endpoints, and scope list. No findings were retrieved, so this must be done before any other step.
gotchas: Do not rely on this guide's placeholder values; confirm each one against Clio's own documentation.

steps.title: Create the OAuth app in Clio's developer console
steps.detail: Sign in to the Clio developer console with your own account and create a new app. Enter the app name you want to show users. Exact menu and field labels are unverified.

steps.title: Set the redirect URI
steps.detail: In the app's OAuth or redirect settings, paste the callback URL from your Composio auth config so the provider sends users back to Composio after authorization.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The URI must match the Composio auth config exactly, including protocol and trailing slash.

steps.title: Choose scopes
steps.detail: Pick the minimum Clio Manage scopes your agent needs and write a one-line justification for each. Scope names and their review tiers were not retrieved, so this step cannot be completed from this guide alone.

steps.title: Copy client credentials into Composio
steps.detail: Copy the client ID and client secret from the Clio app into your Composio auth config for Clio Manage. Store the secret only in Composio, not in code or chat logs.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Connect your own Clio Manage account through Composio. If the authorization succeeds, Gate 1 is reached. Record any error text for the blocker section.

steps.title: Confirm Gate 2 rules for test users
steps.detail: Check whether Clio lets you add invited or test users before public review, and record the user cap and token expiry. This was not covered by the findings.

steps.title: Confirm Gate 3 review requirements
steps.detail: Check whether public use requires review, what the review covers (security, privacy policy, scope justification, demo video), and the expected timeline. Record the answers in this guide before planning a launch.

steps.title: Prepare review materials if required
steps.detail: If Clio requires review, draft the privacy policy, scope justification and app description from the confirmed requirements. Review materials are unknown until Step 9 is complete.

steps.title: Submit for review and wait
steps.detail: Submit the app for review through the Clio console once required materials are ready. Then wait for the provider's decision. Submission process is unverified.

steps.title: Wait for provider decision
steps.detail: Clio's review timeline is unknown. Do not promise end users access until the provider approves the app.
